method.source_voters: Georgia's voter roll as of 2012. Data source is project Mashasadame, originally ran by Jumpstart Georgia and then maintained by ForSet. Original data was provided to Jumpstart Georgia, and then  archived by Davit Bumbeishvili at Awesome Georgian Datasets Github repository (https://github.com/bumbeishvili/awesome-georgian-datasets/blob/master/data/georgian_names_csv.zip)
method.source_book1997: municipal level only, which is why the district toggle is unavailable for it.
method.boundaries_note: Administrative and electoral boundaries were prepared by David Sichinava
method.privacy_intro: A surname in a single precinct can identify a household. Four rules follow, and all four are enforced in the build script rather than in this interface — so the browser never receives anything that needs protecting.
method.privacy_threshold: Any surname × area cell with fewer than {k} people is suppressed and shown as
method.privacy_threshold_2: Suppressed cells are excluded from every ranking and rate.
method.privacy_precinct_lead: Precinct-level counts are never published in any form.
method.privacy_precinct: They exist only inside the build, where they are smoothed into a continuous surface.
method.privacy_kde: The hotspot layer is a kernel density estimate at {km} km bandwidth on a {cols} × {rows} grid, quantised to one byte per cell, with the tail floored to zero. It shows where a surname is dense; it cannot be read back to a count at a point.
method.privacy_complementary: Complementary suppression: because the national total is published, a lone suppressed cell is recoverable by subtraction, so the next-smallest cell is suppressed too.
method.metrics_description: Dashboard shows three metrics: a) count which is a number of records at a national or a regional level; b) a per-1,000 metric and c) concentration, which is a location quotient calculated as:
method.metrics_rate: divides by everyone on the roll in that area.
method.metrics_note: 1 means exactly as common here as everywhere; 6 means six times over-represented.
method.limit_roll_lead: The roll is not the population.
method.limit_roll: No under-18s, no non-citizens, and emigrants often remain listed.
method.limit_1997: Coverage and method differ; treat the change column as directional, not exact.
method.limit_registration: which matters for internally displaced people.
method.limit_boundaries: between 1997 and today; 1997 figures must be apportioned onto current geography before they reach the build.
names.cohort_note: Share of people with this name among voters of the same sex in the 2012 voters list. Years before 1920 are not shown, too few records to be meaningful. Note that the data reflects the electoral list as it stood at publication: people who later emigrated, died, or were added are not accounted for.
names.no_series: No cohort data for this name.
names.map_note: Concentration against the national share. Areas with fewer than {k} bearers are withheld to protect the people in them.
names.suffix_note: Suffix families among people with this first name. The tick marks the same family nationally.
method.names_source: The distribution of first names is based on the 2012 electoral list. Sex comes from public registry data processed by Zviad Kikvidze (https://github.com/zkikvidze/Georgian-Names-By-Gender), matched to each name — it is not a field in the roll itself, so it describes the name rather than the person.
method.names_normalise: Through an administrative inconsistency the same name is often recorded with or without the nominative ending — დავითი and დავით, for instance. The data is normalised to fold these together, but only where the other form actually occurs and the sex matches.
method.names_cohort: The cohort curve shows the share of people carrying a name among those of the same sex born in the same year and registered on the electoral list. Years before 1920 are not included, too few records to be meaningful. The data reflects the position as of 2012.
method.names_suppression: On the maps, names with fewer than {k} bearers in an area are withheld.
